identity.name: Kingdom of Afghanistan
native_names: دولت علیه افغانستان (Dawlat-i ʿAlīyya-yi Afghānistān, 'Sublime State of Afghanistan')
alt_names: Afghanistan under Amanullah, Nadir Shah and Zahir Shah

land.text: the Emirate's whole territory: 'Succeeds Afghan emirate: 9 June 1926'

predecessors.note: Amanullah, already ruler since 1919, took the title of king on 9 June 1926; the emirate dossier (ia-03-e) ends the same day.

land.text: the whole country: 'In July 1973, Daoud Khan staged a bloodless coup d'etat while Zahir Shah was abroad'

successors.note: Zahir Shah abdicated the next month (August 1973); Cliopatria's Republic of Afghanistan row starts in 1973.

capitals.name: Kabul
capitals.note: Infobox lists Kabul, and Jalalabad also for 1929. Habibullah Kalakani held Kabul from 17 January to 13 October 1929 (Afghan Civil War page); Nadir Khan assembled his forces at Jalalabad in March 1929. Coordinates from the gazetteer (the page gives only 33N 65E).

rulers.name: Amanullah Khan
rulers.title: King
rulers.note: King from 9 June 1926; abdicated 14 January 1929 for his brother and fled to British India on 23 May 1929 (Afghan Civil War page).

rulers.name: Inayatullah Khan
rulers.title: King for three days
rulers.note: 14-17 January 1929; surrendered Kabul to Habibullah Kalakani.

rulers.name: Mohammad Nadir Shah
rulers.title: King
rulers.note: 'was proclaimed King of Afghanistan as Mohammad Nadir Shah in October 1929' (accepted the throne on 16 October at Dilkusha, Afghan Civil War page); the Saqqawist emir Habibullah Kalakani held Kabul from January to 13 October 1929. The end year is Zahir Shah's start; the page gives no month. The infobox also lists Mohammad Hashim Khan (a prime minister) among the rulers.

rulers.name: Mohammed Zahir Shah
rulers.title: King
rulers.note: Infobox 1933-1973; deposed by the 17 July 1973 coup of Daoud Khan, abdicated in August.

keyframe_review.note: 644,005 km2 against the infobox 652,864 km2 (for 1973; the body text says 652,200 km2): ratio 0.99. 'Succeeds Afghan emirate: 9 June 1926'; the frontiers are those of the emirate.

Same outline for 1927-1939, but 1929 is not the whole country: Kalakani held Kabul from 17 January to 13 October 1929, then 'Kuhdaman and Kuhistan', and took Kandahar on 31 May or 3 June until 23 September 1929 (events in the ledger). The 1933-1934 frontier adjustment at Arundu and the 3 February 1934 treaty on Dokalim (Durand Line page) are below the grid's 253 km2 cell.
643,832 km2, 173 km2 below the neighbouring shapes (113 vertices against 118); the cell grid is identical. Afghanistan stayed neutral in the Second World War; no territorial change is on the page.
Back to 644,005 km2; identical cells to 1927-1939.

643,906 km2, the same cells. Partition: 'Pakistan inherited the 1893 agreement and the 1919 treaty'; the Durand Line neighbour changes from the British Raj to Pakistan with no land moving. Afghanistan voted against Pakistan's admission to the UN (Kingdom page).

644,005 km2 held to 1968. 'No Afghan government has recognized the Durand Line as its border since 1947' (Durand Line page) but the line did not move. The Wakhan frontier with China was 'delimited in a secret treaty signed on November 1963' (no exchange of land mentioned).
Same outline to 1972; the infobox area 652,864 km2 is for 1973.

correction.text: unchanged outline until the July 1973 coup

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for the last months: the kingdom lasted to the coup of 17 July 1973; Cliopatria's Republic of Afghanistan row takes 1973 onward with the same outline.

region.text: the whole country, the emirate's frontiers

ledger.note: 9 June 1926: Amanullah Khan proclaims the Kingdom of Afghanistan in place of the emirate. Infobox 'Succeeds Afghan emirate: 9 June 1926'; the state is also called the Sublime State of Afghanistan.

region.text: Kabul and the Kuhdaman and Kuhistan areas north of it, held by Kalakani's forces

ledger.note: 17 January 1929: Kabul falls to Habibullah Kalakani. Amanullah 'abdicated in favour of his eldest brother, Inayatullah' on 14 January; 'Inayatullah surrendered and abdicated' on 17 January and 'Kabul fell this day'. Kalakani's side held Kabul and the Kuhdaman and Kuhistan areas (the page names no provinces; Parwan is the researcher's reading).

Late May or early June 1929: Kandahar falls. 'Kalakani's forces took Kandahar after Amanullah's loyalists withdrew' on 31 May (Encyclopaedia Iranica) or 3 June (Faiz Mohammad); Amanullah had left for British India on 23 May.
23 September 1929: Kandahar rises for Nadir. 'A pro-Nadir uprising drove Kalakani's forces out of Kandahar.'

region.text: Kabul and the Kuhdaman and Kuhistan areas north of it, held by Kalakani's forces

ledger.note: 13 October 1929: Nadir Khan retakes Kabul. 'Nadir's forces entered and captured the Arg, ending the civil war'; he reached Kabul on 15 October and, after tribal leaders insisted, accepted the throne on 16 October (Kingdom page: 'proclaimed King of Afghanistan as Mohammad Nadir Shah in October 1929'). Kalakani and ten others were shot on 1 November.

region.text: the whole country passes to the Republic of Afghanistan

ledger.note: 17 July 1973: Daoud Khan overthrows the monarchy. 'In July 1973, Daoud Khan staged a bloodless coup d'etat while Zahir Shah was abroad'; infobox successor Republic of Afghanistan; the king abdicated the next month.

wars.name: Afghan Civil War (1928-1929)

zones.text: Kabul and the Kuhdaman and Kuhistan areas north of it, held by Kalakani's forces

wars.outcome: Shinwari revolt at Jalalabad 14 November 1928; Kalakani attacked Kabul on 14 December and took it on 17 January 1929; Amanullah's Kandahar army failed (retreat from Ghazni 26 April, Kandahar lost 31 May/3 June); Nadir Khan crossed from the Kurram valley on 8 March, took Kabul on 13 October 1929 and was made king; Kalakani was shot on 1 November.
wars.note: The Saqqawist emirate claimed Kandahar, Herat, Turkestan and Qataghan-Badakhshan but its control was 'in a constant state of flux' and never reached Farah or Meymaneh (Emirate of Afghanistan (1929) page, which also lists a Red Army intervention of April-May 1929 without detail).

wars.name: Pashtunistan dispute with Pakistan
wars.outcome: No land changed hands. On 26 July 1949 a loya jirga declared the Durand Line void after a Pakistani air raid on an Afghan-side village; the UK said on 30 June 1950 that Pakistan was the legal heir to the line; Pakistan closed the border in August 1961 (Kingdom page), reopening it the next May.
wars.note: The Durand Line page does not cover the 1960-1961 Bajaur clashes; the border closure comes from the Kingdom page.

certainty.note: The Durand Line was demarcated 1894-1896 and accepted in the treaties of 1919, 1921 and 1930 (Durand Line page); Afghanistan has not recognised it since 1947, but it did not move. The 1929 civil-war fronts (Kabul, Kandahar, the Hazarajat) are soft, the Wakhan frontier with China was delimited only in November 1963, and the Iranian (Helmand) and Soviet (Panj) frontiers were not checked on any page.

notes: Cliopatria draws the whole country for every year, including 1929, when Habibullah Kalakani's Saqqawist 'Emirate of Afghanistan (1929)' held Kabul (17 January-13 October) and Kandahar (31 May/3 June-23 September); the ledger carries those as loss/gain with that rebel state. It lasted under a year, so no rebel dossier was written here; counterparts_needing_dossiers lists emirate-of-afghanistan-1929. The pages dated Kandahar's fall as 31 May (Encyclopaedia Iranica) or 3 June (Faiz Mohammad). Pashtunistan and the Durand Line: the Kingdom's frontier with British India (Raj to 1947) and then Pakistan did not move; the claim of 1947-1961 is a war entry with no zone. The 1960-1961 Bajaur campaign and the Helmand water dispute with Iran are not on the pages opened. No vassal, protectorate or occupation relation appears on the pages opened for 1930-1972; the Soviet Union, British India/Pakistan, Iran and China are neighbours only. The Wakhan corridor (1895 Pamir protocols, Panj frontier) and the Sino-Afghan delimitation of November 1963 are frontier facts (WC page) with no exchange of land. The Dokalim treaty of 3 February 1934 and the Arundu adjustment of 1933-1934 are below the cell size and not entered as gains from british-raj. Not settled: the 1927 rebellion while Amanullah was in Europe (undated), Moqor/Ghazni spring 1929, the Hazarajat in 1929 (Hazara militias held much of it), and the infobox's ruler list (Hashim Khan appears there as 1929-1946 and 1933-1946, and Shah Mahmud Khan, Daoud and Shafiq as rulers, although they were prime ministers). Natural Earth admin-1 names Kabul, Parwan and Kandahar used; no unknown names.
